hints: Focus on what is actually left at equilibrium, not what you started with, by using the mole ratio in the equation.
If 0.8 mol of $\text{SO}_3$ has formed, then 0.8 mol of $\text{SO}_2$ must have reacted and 0.4 mol of $\text{O}_2$ must have reacted.
Work out the total moles left in the mixture and use it to compare partial pressures and to find the mole fraction of $\text{SO}_3$.
walkthrough:
**Set up the equilibrium moles**

Think of this like a recipe. The equation tells you 2 moles of $\text{SO}_2$ react with 1 mole of $\text{O}_2$ to make 2 moles of $\text{SO}_3$.

$$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$$

**Calculate what is left**

You start with 1.0 mol $\text{SO}_2$ and 1.0 mol $\text{O}_2$. To make 0.8 mol $\text{SO}_3$, you must use up 0.8 mol $\text{SO}_2$ and half that amount of $\text{O}_2$, which is 0.4 mol.

Equilibrium moles:
$$n(\text{SO}_2) = 1.0 - 0.8 = 0.2 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{O}_2) = 1.0 - 0.4 = 0.6 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{SO}_3) = 0.8 \text{ mol}$$

**Find the total and the mole fraction**

Add them all together to get the total amount in the closed container.

$$n_{total} = 0.2 + 0.6 + 0.8 = 1.6 \text{ mol}$$

Mole fraction is just share of the total:
$$x(\text{SO}_3) = \frac{0.8}{1.6} = 0.50$$
This is clearly less than 0.8.

**Check the other ideas**

Partial pressure follows mole fraction, so since $n(\text{SO}_2) = 0.2 < n(\text{O}_2) = 0.6$, then $p(\text{SO}_2) < p(\text{O}_2)$. $K_p$ uses partial pressures so it has pressure units like $\text{atm}^{-1}$, never $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$. The forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H$ negative), so cooling shifts equilibrium to the right and makes more $\text{SO}_3$, not less.

options.A: Incorrect. Partial pressure is proportional to moles present. At equilibrium $n(\text{SO}_2)=0.2$ mol and $n(\text{O}_2)=0.6$ mol, so $p(\text{SO}_2)$ is smaller than $p(\text{O}_2)$, not greater.
options.B: Incorrect. $K_p$ is built from partial pressures, so its units involve pressure only. Here $K_p = p(\text{SO}_3)^2 / [p(\text{SO}_2)^2 \times p(\text{O}_2)]$ gives units of $\text{pressure}^{-1}$, e.g. $\text{atm}^{-1}$ or $\text{Pa}^{-1}$. Units of $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ belong to $K_c$.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the opposite of Le Chatelier's principle. The forward reaction is exothermic with $\Delta H = -197 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so lowering temperature favours the exothermic direction and the equilibrium amount of $\text{SO}_3$ would increase above 0.8 mol.
options.D: Correct. Total equilibrium moles = 0.2 + 0.6 + 0.8 = 1.6 mol. Mole fraction of $\text{SO}_3 = 0.8 / 1.6 = 0.5$, which is indeed less than 0.8. Well done for remembering to divide by the total.
